name: Scandinavia in the Viking age
blurb: Small population, no state to speak of, superb shipbuilding and ironworking, and the best long-range mobility in Europe. The opposite problem from Rome: nobody will stop you, and nobody can fund you either.

institutions.note: The thing is an assembly, not a state. No one can license you and no one can fund you.

values._note: Positive w_labour_saving because labour is scarce, not cheap: exactly the reverse of Rome, and the reason a labour-saving machine is welcome here and resented there. Very high w_commerce, high novelty tolerance, and seidr is feared but not prosecuted by a state, because there is no state.
values._note_eminence: No state, no court, nobody to denounce you to. The danger here is a feud, not a treason charge.

hazards.name: Christianisation and political consolidation
hazards.note: changes the value vector rather than killing people

notes: Population is 1.5 million against Rome's 65 million. You will never assemble a large workforce, so every plan must be capital-light and skill-heavy.
Base reach 4: these ships already go to Greenland, the Caspian and Newfoundland. The Atlantic is not a barrier here, which flips the entire expedition branch.
_note_cost_multipliers: The best shipwrights and among the best smiths in Europe, and no state at all. Anything that is a public work rather than a private one costs nearly twice what it costs Rome, because there is nobody to compel or fund it. Concrete is worse still: no pozzolana, no tradition of masonry at scale.

handicap_remedies._doc: The Norse handicap is not skill, it is that there is no body able to compel or fund a public work. Charter one and it goes away.
